note: Rewritten from Silvestri 1914, original in Latin (Contribuzione alla conoscenza dei Termitidi e Termitofili dell'Africa occidentale. I. Termitidi, Bollettino del Laboratorio di Zoologia Generale e Agraria della R. Scuola Superiore d'Agricoltura in Portici 9). Type locality: Kindia, Guinea. The author also establishes the variety var. progrediens (soldier, differences in the antennae), whose Latin description is damaged in the OCR of this volume apart from its opening "Miles. An…", and which is neither translated nor recorded. The page feet are largely missing in the OCR of this passage, and the page given in the locator is inferred from the sequence of the adjacent feet (p. 68—69 and p. 100) and may be off by one page; plate XXXVIII (soldier head, labrum, mandibles, tibia of the second pair of legs) is not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Easily distinguished by the length of the soldier head and the relatively short mandibles: the head is about as long as wide (1.75 versus 0.87 mm, so twice as long as wide), the mandibles are 0.80 mm long, distinctly shorter than the head width, stout, curved and pointed at the tip, with irregular and deeply serrate inner margins. The species is biologically similar to Microcerotermes parvulus.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body cream-coloured, head ochre, mandibles black, abdomen grey and slightly spotted. Head (plate XXXVIII, 1) twice as long as wide, the sides parallel, the posterior corners rounded, the dorsum slightly convex and with a few setae, sloping anteriorly; the base of the labrum slightly wider than long, its anterior margin broadly rounded. Antennae with 13 segments: segment 2 only slightly shorter than segments 3 and 4 together; segment 3 and segment 4 nearly equal in length, segment 3 narrower than segment 4 and the boundary between them indistinct. The mandibles are slightly shorter than the head width, stout, curved and pointed at the tip, their inner margins irregular and rather deeply serrate. The posterior margin of the anterior lobe of the pronotum is slightly concave in the middle. Legs sparsely hairy; the tibia of the second pair of legs (plate XXXVIII, 4) has small but rather stout spines on its outer distal part. The abdomen bears rather many short hairs, with a number of short to rather long hairs also on the posterior margin of each segment. Measurements (mm): body length 5; head length 1.75, head width 0.87; mandible length 0.80; antennal length 1.10; hind tibia 0.65.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Large worker: body straw yellow, head ochre, abdomen with grey spots due to ingested food. The anteclypeus of the head is slightly swollen; antennae with 13 segments, segment 2 slightly shorter than segments 3 and 4 together, segment 3 slightly shorter than segment 4 and with an indistinct boundary to it, paler in colour and usually with only 1—3 outer hairs, segment 5 slightly longer than segment 4. The posterior margin of the anterior lobe of the pronotum is rounded; legs and abdomen as in the soldier. Measurements (mm): body length 4.2; head length 0.91, head width 0.91; antennal length 0.91; hind tibia 0.52. Small worker: antennae with 13 segments, the boundary between segments 3 and 4 usually distinct, segment 3 with several dorsal hairs. Measurements (mm): body length 4; head length 0.68, head width 0.68; antennal length 0.91; hind tibia 0.58.
